title: Bessent Says Tariff Revenue Will Be Little Changed in 2026
summary: Treasury secretary after the Supreme Court ruling: tariff revenue will be little changed because other statutes replace the emergency tariffs, and refunds could be litigated for years.

assertions.quote: the total amount of revenue the Treasury will collect this year will be little changed if changed at all
the existing revenues, you know, under the 230 twos, under the three oh ones and some other collection mechanisms were roughly equal to the EU

verdicts.note: Trade economists estimated the emergency tariffs accounted for roughly two-thirds of 2025 collections, well above the Section 232 and 301 take.

assertions.quote: my sense is that could be dragged out for weeks, months, years

verdicts.note: Customs certified and paid out most of the refunds within months of the ruling.

assertions.quote: There is something called Section 122, which grants the president five months to install to put a global tariff on.

verdicts.note: A ten percent Section 122 tariff was imposed the day of the ruling and succeeded by another global tariff when it expired.

After the Supreme Court ruled in February 2026 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, the fentanyl and reciprocal tariffs were terminated and replaced with a temporary 10 percent surcharge on all imports under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, while Section 232 product tariffs continued.
